result.title: Lossless First-Action Menus for Linear-Reward Planning
result.summary: We study sequential decision making where an agent reserves a minimum menu of initial actions before multi-objective trade-offs are revealed, followed by unrestricted continuation planning once linear reward weights arrive. We prove that a menu preserves the unrestricted optimal return across all linear scalarizations if and only if its reachable continuations cover all vertices of the full feature polytope. This geometric equivalence yields an output-sensitive algorithm that is fixed-parameter tractable in the vertex count, combining scalar backward induction with oracle-based facet identification. On explicitly layered graphs with unit feature increments, menu verification is coNP-complete and synthesis is complete for the second existential level of the polynomial hierarchy, even under additive loss strictly below one. In fixed dimensions two and higher, verification is polynomial whereas synthesis remains NP-complete, while one-dimensional instances admit polynomial-time solutions.

AI.brief_summary: 研究在奖励权重尚未揭示前先保留一个最小的初始动作菜单、之后再自由规划的问题，证明菜单对所有线性标量化保持最优当且仅当其可达后续覆盖特征多面体的全部顶点，并给出以顶点数参数化的算法与若干复杂性结论。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关系，但其「覆盖全部线性标量化顶点以保证无损」的集合式抽象概念，可能为多目标下保留多个候选推理路径或停止选项的表示是否信息无损提供一种可核查的形式化视角。
